name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: China's rare-earth control pause ends 10 Nov with no formal renewal notice
state: China's one-year suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov, and Beijing had published no formal notice extending it as of 5 Nov (Motley Fool). US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the wider US–China truce, extended to 10 Jan 2027, covers the controls, but China's statement did not mention rare earths (Raw Materials). Its April 2025 licensing rules remain in force.
for_you: Manufacturers relying on Chinese rare earths and magnets face possible new licensing delays after 10 Nov. Describes market conditions only; it is not advice.
rubric_hit: Major export controls threatened between large economies = Watch

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
